walkthroughs.body_html:
Your genome is all the DNA in a cell.

DNA is a polymer of two strands forming a double helix, stored in chromosomes in the nucleus. A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a protein.

Genes come in versions called alleles. A dominant allele is expressed if present; a recessive allele only shows when both copies are recessive.

The genotype is the alleles you carry (Bb). The phenotype is what you see (brown eyes).

Variation comes from genes, environment, or both. Mutations create new alleles.

Natural selection: individuals with advantageous alleles survive and reproduce. Over generations this drives evolution.

mcqs.q: Which term describes two identical alleles for a gene?
options: Homozygous
Heterozygous
Phenotype
Recessive

mcqs.q: Where in a cell is DNA mostly found?
options: In the nucleus
In the cytoplasm
In the cell membrane
In the mitochondria only

mcqs.q: What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).
A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.

mcqs.q: What does a gene code for?
options: A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Typically a polypeptide (protein) — through transcription to mRNA and translation by ribosomes.
Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.
A gene codes for a specific physical feature like eye colour directly.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.

mcqs.q: How many chromosomes are in a normal human body cell?
A student crosses two pea plants both heterozygous for height (Tt × Tt), where T (tall) is dominant. Of 80 offspring, roughly how many would be expected to be short?
In a fossil study, older rock layers contain only small horse ancestors and younger layers contain progressively larger horses. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The horse population changed over time, consistent with evolution.
Individual horses grew larger during their own lifetimes.
Larger horses chose to evolve bigger bodies.
The fossils prove evolution does not happen.

mcqs.q: A farmer breeds only the cows that produce the most milk, repeating this for many generations. This is an example of:
options: Selective breeding (artificial selection)
Natural selection
Genetic engineering
A spontaneous mutation

mcqs.q: Bacteria are grown on agar with an antibiotic. A few colonies survive and multiply. Which statement best explains this?
options: A few bacteria had a resistance allele and survived to reproduce.
The antibiotic taught the bacteria how to resist it.
All bacteria became resistant because they needed to.
The surviving bacteria were not exposed to the antibiotic.
